name: Chemistry

requirements.label: 90 Credits Excluding Experiential and Independent Study Courses
requirements.hint: At least 90 credits must come from standard coursework; internships and independent study don't count.

requirements.hint: Credits earned in courses outside the Chemistry department(s).

requirements.label: 90 Credits of Graded Course Work, Including Transfer and Test
requirements.hint: At least 90 credits must carry a letter grade (transfer and test credit included).

requirements.label: 60 Credits of In-Residence Course Work (AA Campus and U-M Study Abroad)
requirements.hint: Credits taken on the Ann Arbor campus or through an approved U-M study abroad program.

requirements.label: 30 Credits Taken While Enrolled in LSA
requirements.hint: Credits earned while officially enrolled in LSA (as opposed to another U-M college).

requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.label: Quantitative Reasoning Requirement
requirements.hint: 1 QR1 or 2 QR2 courses required

requirements.label: Language Requirement
requirements.hint: one 4th term course required, C- minimum, or one course where proficiency is presumed

requirements.hint: From approved HU-designated courses.

requirements.hint: From approved SS-designated courses.

requirements.hint: From approved MSA-designated courses.

requirements.hint: From approved CE-designated courses.

requirements.hint: From approved ID-designated courses.

requirements.label: Chemistry Prerequisites: 5 Credits of Intro Chemistry
requirements.hint: 5 credits of CHEM 125, 126, 130, or approved CHEM electives. No AP or REP credit accepted.

requirements.label: Physics Prerequisites: Intro Physics I with Lab
requirements.hint: 5 credits from PHYSICS (125 and 127), (140 and 141), (150 and 151), (160 and 161), or 139.

requirements.label: Physics Prerequisites: Intro Physics II with Lab
requirements.hint: 5 credits from PHYSICS (240 and 241), (250 and 251), (260 and 261), or 239.

requirements.label: Calculus I
requirements.hint: MATH 115 (or 120) or equivalent.

requirements.label: Calculus II
requirements.hint: MATH 116 (or 121) or equivalent.

requirements.label: Advanced Math: CHEM 262 or MATH Sequence
requirements.hint: Complete either CHEM 262, or MATH 215 plus one of MATH 216 or 217 (or equivalent).

requirements.label: CHEM 262: Mathematical Methods for Physical Scientists
MATH 215 and one of MATH 216 or 217
requirements.hint: 2 courses: must include MATH 215 (Multivariable and Vector Calculus) plus MATH 216 (Differential Equations) or MATH 217 (Linear Algebra).

requirements.label: CHEM 242: Introduction to Chemical Analysis Laboratory
Physical Chemistry Intro: CHEM (230 and 261) or 260
requirements.hint: Complete either CHEM 260, or both CHEM 230 and CHEM 261.

requirements.label: CHEM 230 and CHEM 261
requirements.hint: Both CHEM 230 (Physical Chemical Principles and Applications) and CHEM 261 (Introduction to Quantum Chemistry).

requirements.label: Inorganic Chemistry: CHEM 302 or 303
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: CHEM 302 (Inorganic Chemistry: Molecules, Materials and Applications in Energy) or CHEM 303 (Introductory Bioinorganic Chemistry).

requirements.label: Advanced Lecture Courses
requirements.hint: 3 of the following: CHEM 215, 351, 402, 447, and CHEM 461 or 463 (only one of 461 and 463 may count).

requirements.label: Advanced Laboratory Courses
requirements.hint: 3 of the following: CHEM 216, 436, 462, 482, 483.

requirements.label: Major Total: 40 Credits
requirements.hint: Includes all courses used toward the major requirements; prerequisites do not count. Reach 40 with additional approved 300-level or higher CHEM electives, including undergrad research (CHEM 399/499) and honors thesis. No more than 4 credits of CHEM 398/399 may be used, and electives may not repeat courses used for advanced lecture or lab.
